rationale: Migration 642 (applied 2026-08-26, portfolio_positioning lane): the deploy-path half of SEO-002's open question, deferred by 590's own header. 590 deferred it with a costing that was right about the wrong design: 'the deploy path would re-probe a whole site on every page change (135 requests for webdesign.co.uk, every time)'. Firing a render PER EDIT is expensive, but the rotation already carries a hard cost cap — one site per 1800s tick, max 48 renders/day fleet-wide — so the deploy-path event belongs in the SELECTOR, where the cap already lives, not in a new dispatch path. 642 adds one OR-branch to sitemap-refresh-rotation's pre_query: a site becomes due EARLY when any pages row changed since its last render (updated_at > last_selected_at), gated by a 30-minute quiet period so a rerender wave settles into one render instead of a mid-wave render plus a second one after. The 3-day line becomes an unconditional FLOOR: the quiet test gates only the early branch, so a site edited for ever still gets its floor refresh — silent never-selection is the drift mode 622 was written to refuse, and this preserves that argument. Why updated_at alone: surveyed 2026-08-26, every UPDATE pages statement in the Go tree bumps updated_at=NOW() alongside what it changes (deploy stamp deploy_evidence.go:294, retraction, needs_rebuild, section stores — 12 call sites) and 0 rows fleet-wide have updated_at < deployed_at, so one column covers new-page deploy, redeploy, retraction, noindex flip and expiry-set without the pre_query naming any visibility column (which 622's verify forbids as the mirror that drifts). Latency: a published or retracted page waited up to 3 days to reach the sitemap; now 30-60 minutes typical. The behavioural proof is built into the apply moment: all 31 stamps are 2026-08-24/25, so under the old rule zero sites are due before 2026-08-27 16:02:34 — any selection before that instant can only be the new branch, and at apply time 20 sites were due-by-change-and-quiet (apply NOTICE: '0 by age, 20 by change-and-quiet').

plan.summary: One anchored surgical edit to scheduled_tasks.pre_query for sitemap-refresh-rotation (migration 642 + ROLLBACK, both files new). The 3-day due test becomes '(3-day floor) OR (changed-since-render AND 30-min quiet)'. Pre-flight asserts the anchor's OCCURRENCE count is exactly 1 (the 622 editquality lesson: replace() is global and a row count says nothing about occurrences within a row) and refuses a double apply. The verify block asserts POST-state occurrence counts for all three clauses, asserts 622's has-deployed-pages guard is still exactly-once, the locked_at guard survives, and no visibility column (pg.noindex/pg.expires_at) has appeared; then EXECUTEs the live due-predicate and NOTICEs both branch counts.
plan.risks: (1) Over-trigger: pre-deploy content edits bump updated_at and buy a render that changes nothing served. Accepted deliberately — mid-build sites are already excluded by the claimed-build guard, cost is capped by the tick, and the safe failure direction for this selector is render-too-often, never never-render (622's argument). (2) Wave saturation: a fleet rerender wave (27 sites touched 2026-08-25) makes most sites due; the tick drains 31 sites in ~15.5h. Bounded and cheap (~26 GETs per render average, 147 max, measured 2026-08-26). (3) Empty-diff commits: an identical re-render pushes an empty-diff 'Update sitemap.xml' commit — the git adapter's no-op skip covers deletions only (github_client.go:250). Rare (needs two same-day renders with no lastmod movement), succeeds, fails no run. (4) Quiet-period starvation is structurally refuted, not merely unlikely: the 3-day floor branch carries no quiet requirement, so the worst a permanently-busy site can suffer is exactly today's behaviour.

edits.rationale: The change itself: anchored replace of the single 3-day due line with the floor-OR-early-branch block, with occurrence-count pre-flight (anchor exactly once, refuse double apply) and occurrence-count verify (each new clause exactly once; 622's guard, locked_at, and the no-visibility-column invariants preserved; live due counts NOTICEd).
edits.sketch:
AND (
  COALESCE(r.last_selected_at, '-infinity'::timestamptz) < now() - interval '3 days'
  OR (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pages pu WHERE pu.site_id = s.id AND pu.updated_at > r.last_selected_at)
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pages pq WHERE pq.site_id = s.id AND pq.updated_at > now() - interval '30 minutes'))
)

edits.rationale: Reverse replace of the whole inserted block back to the plain 3-day line, with its own exactly-once pre-flight on the block and post-state assertions that the early branch is gone, the plain line is back exactly once, and 622/locked_at guards survived the rollback.
edits.sketch: UPDATE scheduled_tasks SET pre_query = replace(pre_query, v_new_block, v_old_line) WHERE name='sitemap-refresh-rotation'; -- then assert absence of 'interval ''30 minutes''' and exactly-once of the old line

grounded_in: 590 header, the deferral being closed: 'the deploy path would re-probe a whole site on every page change (135 requests for webdesign.co.uk, every time). The deploy-path half is left for a second, separate change, once this one is proven at the artefact.'

622 header, the drift argument this preserves: 'A guard that cannot be wrong in the dangerous direction beats a guard that is currently exact' — and its verify RAISEs if pg.noindex or pg.expires_at appear in the pre_query; 642's verify re-asserts both absences.

deploy_evidence.go:285-295 (buildPageDeployStampQuery): the deploy stamp writes 'deployed_at = NOW(), ... updated_at = NOW()' in one statement — measured 2026-08-26: 0 rows fleet-wide have updated_at < deployed_at, so updated_at subsumes deployed_at as the change signal.
cmd/scheduler/main.go (runPreQuery no-rows branch): 'The pre-query ran and found nothing to do. That is a successful no-op, not a skip' — a tick with nothing due costs nothing and breaks nothing.

Churn measured 2026-08-26 (pages.updated_at, distinct sites/day): 2026-08-19: 2, 08-20: 2, 08-21: 1, 08-22: 0, 08-23: 3, then 08-25: 27 and 08-26 (to 09:30 BST): 21 — normal churn is a few sites/day, waves are episodic; the quiet period plus tick cap is sized against the wave case.
